annotations.text:
The restructure: context on the left, work in the middle, the verdict on the right.

Today everything is one scroll — the numbers you came for sit mid-page and the reasons they might be wrong sit at the very bottom, below the fold. Here the chromatogram that governs the whole analysis stays pinned, and Rg / fit quality / insights never scroll away.
Guinier and residuals now share one card, because they share an x-axis — the residuals are how you judge the fit, so they belong next to it, not three sections down.

Chart colour does two separate jobs and today they collide: green currently means both 'in the fit' and 'qRg is fine'.

Split here — teal ramp = what you selected, status trio = whether to trust it. Both sets were run through the palette validator; the current palette fails it on chroma and contrast.
Two alternate structures, kept low-fi on purpose — enough to choose between, not to build from. Say if either is closer and I'll take it up to the fidelity of the workspace artboard.

Values shown are sample data from a synthetic lysozyme-like SEC run, not real measurements — plots are generated from a sphere form factor with Rg 24.8 Å so the five charts stay physically consistent with each other.
